disclaimer: This information is for general educational purposes regarding commonly available over-the-counter (OTC) supportive remedies. It does NOT constitute a prescription, medical diagnosis, or personalized pharmacological advice. Never administer medications to infants or children without consulting a pediatrician. Always read the product package leaflet, follow manufacturer instructions, and consult a registered doctor or pharmacist before taking any medication.
notice: All medicines and supportive measures listed are general OTC supportive options only. No prescription-only medicines (POM) or antibiotics are recommended. Dosage, safety warnings, and contraindications must always be verified on the packaging or directly with a licensed healthcare professional.

fever.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
fever.purpose: Reduces body temperature (antipyretic) and relieves associated mild to moderate pain or body aches.
fever.general_info: Common first-line over-the-counter antipyretic and analgesic. Available in tablet, capsule, and oral suspension forms. Helps lower elevated body temperature by acting on the hypothalamus heat-regulating center.
precautions: Do not exceed the maximum daily adult dose stated on the product package (typically 4000 mg in 24 hours from all sources).
Check labels of all concurrent medications (such as multi-symptom cold syrups) to prevent accidental paracetamol overdose.
Maintain an interval of at least 4 to 6 hours between individual doses.
Always use the measuring syringe or cup provided with liquid formulations rather than household kitchen spoons.
avoid_if: Known severe allergy or hypersensitivity to paracetamol or acetaminophen.
Severe liver impairment, active liver disease, or acute liver failure.
Chronic heavy alcohol consumption or alcohol-related liver injury.
fever.note: Safe and effective when used strictly as directed. Seek pediatric consultation for age-appropriate child formulations; never administer adult dosage strengths to children.

cold_cough.name: Paracetamol
cold_cough.purpose: Relieves body aches, fever, and headache associated with common cold or respiratory viral infections.
cold_cough.general_info: Over-the-counter pain reliever and fever reducer that eases general malaise and muscular discomfort during a viral upper respiratory infection.
precautions: Ensure total paracetamol intake across all cold and flu combination products does not exceed the manufacturer daily adult limit.
Allow at least 4 to 6 hours between doses.
Consult a doctor if fever lasts more than 3 days or symptoms worsen.
avoid_if: Known allergy or hypersensitivity to paracetamol.
Severe liver disease or hepatic impairment.
Chronic severe alcoholism.
cold_cough.note: Does not cure viral infections or suppress cough directly, but improves overall comfort during illness.

cold_cough.name: Steam Inhalation
cold_cough.purpose: Moistens respiratory airways, relieves nasal congestion, and loosens viscous bronchial mucus.
cold_cough.general_info: A natural non-pharmacological supportive therapy using warm water vapor to soothe irritated nasal passages and facilitate airway drainage.
precautions: Keep facial skin at a safe distance (at least 20 to 30 cm) from the hot water surface to avoid accidental steam burns or scalds.
Keep boiling water and electrical steamers completely out of reach of children.
Inhale slowly and steadily through the nose for 5 to 10 minutes at a time.
avoid_if: Unsupervised young children or individuals with reduced sensory sensation or cognitive impairment.
Severe acute asthma exacerbation where hot vapor may trigger reactive bronchospasm.
cold_cough.note: Plain water steam is effective and gentle; avoid adding concentrated essential oils which can irritate delicate respiratory mucosa.

cold_cough.name: Saline Nasal Drops
cold_cough.purpose: Hydrates nasal mucous membranes and gently thins mucus to clear congested nasal passages.
cold_cough.general_info: Sterile 0.9% sodium chloride isotonic saline solution available over the counter as drops or spray. Free from active drug chemicals or decongestants.
precautions: Do not share nasal droppers or spray bottles with other family members to avoid cross-infection.
Discard open saline solution containers according to manufacturer expiration timelines to preserve sterility.
Gently blow or wipe the nose after administration.
avoid_if: Any known allergy to added preservatives (if using preserved formulas; use preservative-free saline instead).
Severe facial trauma or suspected skull base fracture.
cold_cough.note: Non-addictive and does not cause rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa), making it suitable for frequent supportive daily use.

headache.name: Paracetamol
headache.purpose: Relieves mild to moderate tension headaches and discomfort.
headache.general_info: Widely used OTC analgesic that acts on the central nervous system to reduce pain sensation without causing gastric mucosal irritation.
precautions: Do not combine with other medications containing paracetamol.
Adhere strictly to recommended adult doses on the packaging.
Limit frequent regular use to prevent medication-overuse (rebound) headaches.
avoid_if: Severe hepatic impairment or active liver disease.
Known hypersensitivity to paracetamol.
Concomitant heavy alcohol consumption.
headache.note: Gentle on the stomach and preferred for individuals with a history of acid reflux or stomach ulcers.

headache.name: Ibuprofen
headache.purpose: Reduces pain and inflammatory swelling associated with tension headaches, sinus headaches, and muscular soreness.
headache.general_info: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that inhibits prostaglandin synthesis to alleviate inflammatory pain.
precautions: Always take with or immediately after food or a glass of milk to protect the stomach lining.
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration necessary.
Stay well hydrated while taking NSAIDs to support renal clearance.
Consult a physician before use if you have hypertension or cardiovascular conditions.
avoid_if: Active stomach ulcers, history of gastrointestinal bleeding, or severe gastritis.
Severe kidney dysfunction or chronic renal disease.
Third trimester of pregnancy.
Aspirin-sensitive asthma or known NSAID hypersensitivity.
Concurrent use of anticoagulant or blood-thinning medications without medical supervision.
headache.note: Do not take concurrently with other NSAIDs (such as naproxen, diclofenac, or aspirin).

sore_throat.name: Warm Saline Gargle
sore_throat.purpose: Reduces pharyngeal tissue edema, washes away accumulated secretions, and eases localized throat pain.
sore_throat.general_info: A gentle hypertonic/isotonic home rinse made by dissolving 1/2 teaspoon of table salt in a glass of warm clean water.
precautions: Ensure water temperature is comfortably lukewarm, never scalding hot.
Gargle in the back of the throat for 20 to 30 seconds and spit out completely; do not swallow.
Repeat 3 to 4 times daily as needed.
avoid_if: Young children who cannot yet reliably spit out fluids without choking or swallowing.
Individuals with severe swallowing impairment (dysphagia).
sore_throat.note: A simple, highly effective, drug-free supportive remedy that can be used safely alongside other supportive measures.

sore_throat.name: Throat Lozenges
sore_throat.purpose: Soothes raw throat lining and provides temporary localized relief from throat irritation and swallowing pain.
sore_throat.general_info: Hard dissolvable pastilles containing soothing agents (such as pectin, glycerin, honey, or mild cooling menthol) that stimulate salivation.
precautions: Allow the lozenge to dissolve slowly in the mouth without chewing or biting.
Keep out of reach of toddlers and small children due to potential choking hazard.
Check sugar content if managing diabetes; sugar-free alternatives are available.
avoid_if: Children under 4 to 6 years of age who have choking vulnerability.
Known allergy to any specific flavor, dye, or active ingredient in the lozenge.
sore_throat.note: Provides temporary topical comfort; does not treat underlying bacterial or viral pathogens.

sore_throat.name: Warm Fluids with Honey
sore_throat.purpose: Coats and lubricates the irritated pharyngeal mucosa, providing natural soothing relief and easing tickly coughs.
sore_throat.general_info: A traditional supportive home remedy combining warm water or caffeine-free herbal tea with a spoonful of pure honey.
precautions: Ensure fluid is pleasantly warm, not hot enough to scald mouth or throat tissues.
Rinse mouth or brush teeth before bed if consuming sweet fluids to protect dental enamel.
avoid_if: Infants under 12 months of age (STRICT CONTRAINDICATION due to the risk of infant botulism caused by Clostridium botulinum spores).
sore_throat.note: Scientifically supported as an effective demulcent for cough and throat irritation in adults and children over 1 year of age.

stomach.name: ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)
stomach.purpose: Prevents and treats mild to moderate dehydration and electrolyte depletion caused by diarrhea or vomiting.
stomach.general_info: A scientifically balanced formulation of glucose and electrolytes (sodium, potassium, chloride, citrate) conforming to WHO rehydration standards.
precautions: Dissolve the sachet in the exact volume of clean drinking water specified on the packet (do not use milk, juice, or soda).
Sip slowly in small, frequent amounts (a teaspoon or small sip every few minutes) to prevent triggering nausea.
Discard prepared solution after 24 hours if kept at room temperature (or after 48 hours if refrigerated).
avoid_if: Severe intestinal obstruction, paralytic ileus, or intractable vomiting requiring IV rehydration.
Severe kidney failure with hyperkalemia, unless specifically directed by a nephrologist.
stomach.note: Crucial first-line supportive therapy for any gastrointestinal fluid loss; rehydrates far more effectively than plain water alone.

stomach.name: Antacid
stomach.purpose: Rapidly neutralizes excess gastric acid to relieve heartburn, sour stomach, and acid indigestion.
stomach.general_info: Over-the-counter chewable tablets or liquid suspensions containing basic salts like magnesium hydroxide, aluminum hydroxide, or calcium carbonate.
precautions: Take 1 to 2 hours after meals or at bedtime as directed by product instructions.
Separate antacid intake by at least 2 hours from other medications, as antacids can reduce drug absorption.
Chew tablets thoroughly before swallowing and follow with a glass of water.
avoid_if: Severe chronic kidney disease (risk of magnesium or aluminum accumulation).
Hypercalcemia (for calcium-based antacids).
Severe unexplained acute abdominal pain or suspected appendicitis.
stomach.note: Intended for occasional, short-term symptomatic acid relief. Consult a doctor if heartburn occurs regularly more than twice a week.

general.name: Paracetamol
general.purpose: Provides supportive relief for mild general body aches, muscle stiffness, and elevated body temperature.
general.general_info: Standard first-line over-the-counter analgesic and antipyretic for general malaise and fever management.
precautions: Adhere strictly to manufacturer packaging limits and avoid taking multiple paracetamol-containing products simultaneously.
Maintain 4 to 6 hours between individual doses.
Stay well hydrated while resting.
avoid_if: Severe liver dysfunction or chronic heavy alcohol consumption.
Known hypersensitivity to paracetamol.
general.note: A dependable, well-tolerated supportive remedy for general discomfort when taken according to directions.

general.name: ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)
general.purpose: Restores vital electrolyte balance and hydration during periods of physical exhaustion, heat stress, or mild illness.
general.general_info: WHO-formulated electrolyte and glucose mixture that optimizes cellular water and electrolyte uptake through sodium-glucose cotransport.
precautions: Mix with the exact amount of boiled and cooled or clean filtered water indicated on the package.
Consume throughout the day in small frequent sips.
Do not add extra sugar, salt, or flavorings to pre-measured packets.
avoid_if: Severe dehydration with circulatory shock (requires immediate emergency medical intervention and IV fluids).
Significant renal insufficiency or severe electrolyte imbalances requiring hospital monitoring.
general.note: Maintains essential fluid and electrolyte balance during recovery from physical fatigue, heat exposure, or illness.
